rationale: M=32 is fixed (only block_M=32 divides M, and prior plan exposed 32/64 but 64 cannot tile M=32; removed 64 to keep MIP candidates feasible for this tall-skinny GEMM). N=4096, K=4096 remain divisible by chosen N and K values. Kept num_stages 1-3 and threads=128; shared-memory estimate 2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages stays within 49152 for all candidates (max 32+128, K=64, stages=3 = 61440 exceeds budget, so footprint constraint will prune the largest tile/stage combination). Prior selection block_M=32, block_N=64, block_K=32, num_stages=2 had smem=12288, 62 registers, reg cap fine, simulator estimated ~147.8us with dram near-saturated (99%) and tensor busy 0.36 — suggesting memory bound and small tile_M limiting A-reuse; larger block_N (128) or block_K (64) with fewer stages may reduce DRAM pressure and launches, so footprint and traffic weights were raised and launches lowered to let MIP explore those. Feedback is a single verified compile+simulation point; CPU-shadow correctness and latency do NOT establish CUDA correctness or GB10 performance, simulator values are model estimates only, and no checked GPU results or SASS timing claims are inferred.
